problems.title: Equal arithmetic partial sums
problems.question: If S₁₀=S₂₀ in an arithmetic progression, what must hold?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: Equating the sums gives 2a₁+29d=0, so a₁=−29d/2.
Therefore a₁d=−29d²/2<0 when d≠0. If d=0, the equality instead forces a₁=0.
problems.note: The printed strict inequality needs d≠0. The zero progression satisfies the premise and violates it, so none of the listed claims holds universally as written.

problems.title: Five numbers with four prescribed statistics
problems.question: How many unordered natural-number five-tuples have unique mode, median, mean and range all equal to 5?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Sorted entries have middle 5, sum 25 and last−first=5.
steps: The minimum is m≤5 and maximum m+5. Since 5 must repeat, enumerate m=1,2,3,4,5 under the sum constraint.
For m=1, the other three entries must sum 18, but including at least two 5s cannot give unique mode 5 with the required order and total.
For m=2 the only valid tuple is (2,5,5,6,7); for m=3 it is (3,4,5,5,8). For m≥4 the total is at least 4+4+5+5+9=27.
problems.note: Tuples are counted as data sets in sorted order; counting ordered arrangements would give a different count.

problems.title: A finite geometric ratio
problems.question: A finite geometric progression starts at 1, ends at 16√2, and has sum 31/(√2−1). Find its ratio.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: For q=√2 the numerator is 16√2·√2−1=31, matching the sum.
Indeed the terms run from (√2)⁰ to (√2)⁹, so the endpoint and term count agree.

problems.question: Nonzero vectors satisfy |a+b|=|a−b|. What angle do they form?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: For nonzero vectors a·b=|a||b|cosθ, so cosθ=0.

problems.title: Exponentiate an arithmetic progression
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has a₁=1,d=−2. Find 5^a₁+5^a₂+⋯.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The powered terms form a geometric progression with first term 5 and ratio 5^(−2)=1/25.
steps: The ratio has absolute value below 1.

problems.title: A false event identity
problems.question: On a die, A means even, B prime, C impossible and D certain. Which listed identity is false?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: A∩B={2}, which is not the empty set C.
The remaining identities follow from union with the whole space, intersection with the empty set, and complementary events.

problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Collinear nonzero vectors are scalar multiples.
steps: The determinant ux·vy−uy·vx is nonzero for each other pair.

problems.title: Perpendicular medians determine an angle
problems.question: CA=4,CB=6, and medians AD,BE are perpendicular. Find cosC.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Take C as origin with vectors u=CA,v=CB. Then (v/2−u)·(u/2−v)=0.

problems.title: Primitive arithmetic triangle sides
problems.question: Natural triangle sides form an arithmetic progression, one angle is 120°, and their gcd is 1. Find the perimeter.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Write sides m−d,m,m+d, with largest side opposite 120°.
steps: Simplifying gives m=5d, so the sides are 4d,5d,6d.
Their gcd is d=1; the perimeter is 4+5+6.

problems.title: The same three numbers in two progressions
problems.question: Three numbers can be arranged as both an arithmetic and a geometric progression. Find geometric ratio q if |q|>1.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Write the geometric terms t,tq,tq², t≠0. One must be the average of the other two.
steps: Equating twice the middle-sized candidate to the other two gives (q−1)²=0, or (q−1)(q+2)=0, or (q−1)(2q+1)=0.
The possible nonconstant ratios are −2 and −1/2. Only −2 has magnitude above 1.
problems.note: If all three numbers are zero, a geometric ratio is not uniquely defined. The usual nonzero progression assumption is needed.

problems.title: A false progression sum formula
problems.question: Identify the incorrect formula among the printed arithmetic and geometric sum formulas.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: The formula Pₙ=(b₁+bₙ)/(q−1) omits the factor q on the final term and uses addition instead of subtraction.
For example b₁=1,q=2,n=2 gives actual sum 3 but the proposed formula also3 by coincidence; n=3 gives actual7 and proposed5, disproving it.

problems.title: A line through the midpoint of an altitude
problems.question: In isosceles ABC, AB=BC=5,AC=6. K is midpoint of altitude BD. In what ratio does AK divide BC from B?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: Write a point on BC as (3t,4−4t). A point on AK has equation y=(2/3)(x+3).
The two lengths on BC have ratio t:(1−t).

problems.title: Distance between parallel lines
problems.question: Find the distance between 4x+3y−1=0 and 8x+6y+3=0.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: Divide the second equation by 2 to get 4x+3y+1.5=0.

problems.question: Which listed point lies on both (x−1)²+y²=4 and (x+1)²+y²=4?

steps: Both intersections are (0,±√3); only the positive one is listed.

steps: Only the final product is negative.
